title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
authors_or_org: Yunfan Gao, Yun Xiong, Xinyu Gao, Kangxiang Jia, Jinliu Pan, Yuxi Bi, Yi Dai, Jiawei Sun, Meng Wang, Haofen Wang (Tongji + Fudan)
key_takeaways: Taxonomy of three RAG paradigms: Naive, Advanced, Modular; Modular adds Search, Memory, Routing, Predict, Task-Adapter modules
Inventories 26 downstream tasks, ~50 datasets, evaluation objectives and metrics for RAG
Cross-references most other RAG papers (RAPTOR, Self-RAG, FLARE, REPLUG, HyDE, ITER-RETGEN, DSP, RECITE)

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors_or_org: Xiaohua Wang et al. (Fudan University, FudanDNN-NLP)
key_takeaways: Empirical ablation across 7 RAG modules on TREC DL19/20, MS MARCO, lyft_2021
BAAI LLM-Embedder beats text-embedding-ada-002 on cost/quality and is selected as default
HyDE + hybrid search lifts nDCG@10 from 50.58 (BM25) to 73.34 on TREC DL19 but at 11.16s latency
Milvus is the only evaluated vector DB satisfying multi-index, billion-scale, hybrid search, cloud-native
Sentence-level chunking with chunk_size 256-512 and 20-token overlap maximizes faithfulness/relevancy

title: PipeRAG: Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Algorithm-System Co-design
authors_or_org: Wenqi Jiang, Shuai Zhang, Boran Han, Jie Wang, Bernie Wang, Tim Kraska (Amazon / MIT)
key_takeaways: Pipeline-parallelizes retrieval with generation by accepting a stale query window; up to 2.6x latency speedup over Retro at iso-perplexity
Performance-model-driven ANN search picks max nprobe such that retrieval latency hides under the next-chunk inference latency
Periodic retrieval beats one-shot retrieval; perplexity drops as database scales toward the full C4 corpus
Note: seed.yaml listed 2403.05676 as 'Searching for Best Practices' - that title actually lives at 2407.01219; this arXiv ID is PipeRAG

title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
authors_or_org: Nouha Dziri et al. (AI2, UW, USC, UChicago)
key_takeaways: Off-the-shelf ChatGPT and GPT-4 hit only 55% and 59% on 3-digit x 3-digit multiplication
Transformers solve compositional tasks by linearized subgraph matching, not systematic decomposition; OOD generalization fails
Theoretical: error probability for n-step compositions converges exponentially to 1 - relevant to multi-hop RAG pipelines
Note: seed.yaml labeled this arXiv ID as FActScore; the real FActScore is 2305.14251. This paper is unrelated to faithfulness eval but informs multi-hop limits

title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors_or_org: Shahul Es, Jithin James, Luis Espinosa-Anke, Steven Schockaert (Exploding Gradients / Cardiff NLP)
key_takeaways: Reference-free metrics: Faithfulness = |verified statements|/|total statements|; Answer Relevance = mean cos(q, q_i) over LLM-generated reverse questions; Context Relevance = relevant sentences / total sentences
Uses gpt-3.5-turbo-16k as judge; aligns with human pairwise judgements at 0.95 (faith), 0.78 (ans rel), 0.70 (ctx rel) on WikiEval
Decomposes long answers into atomic statements before verifying each against retrieved context (faithfulness primitive)

title: Contextual Retrieval in AI Systems
key_takeaways: Add LLM-generated chunk-specific context (50-100 tokens) before embedding+indexing
Contextual Embeddings alone -35% top-20 failure rate (5.7% to 3.7%)
+Contextual BM25 -49% (5.7% to 2.9%)
+Reranker -67% (5.7% to 1.9%)
Indexing cost: prompt-cached chunk-context generation

title: Cohere Rerank 3.5 model card
key_takeaways: Rerank 3.5 on reasoning data: 81.59% retrieval accuracy vs BM25 43.53%, Dense 50.64%, Hybrid 48.80%
Multilingual nDCG@10: Rerank 3.5 62.18% vs Dense 53.83%, Hybrid 52.10%, BM25 38.19%
+23.4% over Hybrid Search on financial dataset

title: Qdrant Indexing concepts
key_takeaways: Payload indexes MUST be created before data ingestion for filterable HNSW edges
Filtered queries can be blocked on unindexed fields (strict mode) for predictable latency
On-disk payload index trades cold latency for memory savings

title: Cohere Rerank reference architecture
key_takeaways: Reference pattern: BM25 top-100 -> rerank to top-N (typically top-3 or top-10)
Top-100 candidate window is the standard rerank input size

title: An LLM-as-Judge Won't Save The Product - Fixing Your Process Will
key_takeaways: Eval is an engineering control loop, not a leaderboard
Hypothesize -> experiment -> measure -> iterate
Calibrate automated evaluators against human annotation

title: A Field Guide to Rapidly Improving AI Products
key_takeaways: The single most impactful investment is a custom data viewer for AI traces
Generic dashboards underperform domain-specific viewers
Use synthetic data strategically to bootstrap eval before real users

title: LLM Evals: Everything You Need to Know (FAQ)
key_takeaways: RAG = retrieval search problem + generation problem; evaluate separately
Retrieval: Recall@K, Precision@K, MRR; Generation: error analysis + LLM-judge validated against human labels
Do not use off-the-shelf judge prompts; iterate based on observed failure modes

title: The RAG Eval Antipattern That Hides Retriever Bugs
key_takeaways: End-to-end eval lets generator hide retriever bugs for months
Recall@K < 0.5-0.6 -> retriever is the bottleneck
Precision@K < 0.4 -> retriever is adding too much noise

title: Stop Building Against Gold Datasets
key_takeaways: Production data is messier than any curated benchmark
Chasing high pass rates means tests are too easy
70% on meaningful production evals > 95% on irrelevant benchmark
